As per the How Does PoisonTap Work section, apparently it presents itself as a USB network interface, which does get trusted by default. When the new interface tries to set itself up via DHCP, it gives its subnet mask indicating that it owns the entire IPv4 address space (0.0.0.0/32 instead of just say 192.168.1.0/8). The subnet of even a low priority device trumps the gateway settings of even the highest priority, and bam. All traffic is now routed through it.

Sneaky, sneaky, very sneaky.
